generatedProse.concept-context: Across the School of Sport the conventions of writing are specific, and they are not the same from one subject to the next. In sport and exercise science the writing follows a structured report format, with introduction, method, results and discussion, and a cautious, impersonal register. Claims are hedged and tied to the data of a study or a physiological test. A coaching student writing a reflective account, or a management student writing a participation case, works to different conventions again. What stays constant is that your writing is judged against your own subject's conventions, not a single universal standard.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two final-year sport and exercise science students make the same point, that a physiology finding should be read with caution, in a lab report.

Tom writes it the way it might be written in any subject: 'I think this result is quite interesting, but I am not sure we can fully trust it.' The point is there, but the register is personal and informal. Sport and exercise science expects claims to be hedged and tied to the data, with the writer kept in the background, so it reads as unsupported.

Amara writes the same caution in the conventions of the subject: 'The effect is sizeable, but its basis in a single, well-trained sample limits how far it can be generalised.' The judgement is identical. What differs is that Amara has used the subject's cautious vocabulary, its impersonal voice, and its habit of grounding a claim in a specific limitation of the study.

Both students reached the same judgement. Only Amara expressed it in the conventions sport and exercise science is marked against.
generatedProse.summary: Academic writing in the School of Sport is not one skill but a set of conventions each subject sets for structure, register and the handling of evidence. You can now explain why there is no monolithic academic writing, analyse how sport and exercise science differs from a subject such as coaching, and begin to identify a subject's conventions. The next lesson turns recognition into method: how to work those conventions out from the writing the School of Sport already publishes.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara's version read as sport and exercise science writing rather than generic?

items.text: She used the subject's cautious, impersonal register and grounded the claim in a specific limitation of the study.
She reached a more cautious judgement than Tom did.
She wrote a longer sentence than Tom.
She avoided mentioning the study's data at all.

feedback.correct: That's right. Same judgement, expressed in sport and exercise science's conventions and tied to a specific limitation.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. The two judgements were the same; look at HOW Amara expressed hers.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara's version read as sport and exercise science writing because she used the subject's cautious, impersonal register and grounded the claim in a specific limitation, not because it was longer or more cautious.
